clue.text: But you can't cut celery with them!

definitions.text: But you can't cut celery with them!

blocks.clueFragment: But you can't cut celery with them!
blocks.note: surface reading: some kitchen implements are useless for slicing vegetables
setter's reading: what you do to celery with a knife, said in two words, is also the name of the eating implements meant

explanation.surface: A cook complains that some utensil is no good for preparing celery.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer split in two reads CHOP STICKS, exactly what you would do to celery, yet these slender eating tools could never do it.
explanation.definitionFit: They are the pair of thin wooden or plastic sticks used for eating in East Asian cuisine, useless as a blade.

indicators.note: something distressed is knocked about and damaged, so the letters that follow are broken up and rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written, though it reads as joining the emu to the floor

explanation.surface: A sick, upset emu lies on the floor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' does double duty here: it reads as linking the emu to the floor, but its letters are needed in the anagram fodder along with EMU ILL.
explanation.definitionFit: Linoleum is a hard-wearing sheet material laid over floors, made from linseed oil and cork on a backing.

indicators.note: in a down clue, soaring means going upwards, so the word for the birds is read from the bottom up

blocks.note: taken as written
emus are large flightless Australian birds

explanation.surface: Something is donned as the birds take to the sky.
explanation.walkthrough: The joke is that the birds chosen are emus, which cannot soar at all except in a down entry, where they rise from the bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: To put on an air, a manner or a garment is to assume it, a standard synonym in this sense.

blocks.note: first meaning: the ancient Phoenician port in what is now Lebanon
second meaning: the rubber ring fitted round a wheel

explanation.surface: A musical group named after an ancient town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'band' suggests musicians, but here it is a ring or hoop of rubber round a wheel.
explanation.definitionFit: Tyre was a great Phoenician seaport, and a tyre is the circular rubber band around a vehicle's wheel.

blocks.note: surface reading: someone in charge of some group sets the schedule
setter's reading: the master of these is the familiar compere who runs a formal event

explanation.surface: A boss controls the order of events in a schedule.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase 'master of ceremonies' is the key: the compere or MC who announces each item in turn at a dinner or show.
explanation.definitionFit: Formal occasions such as banquets and prize-givings are run in order by a master of ceremonies, so these are the events he presides over.

indicators.note: fighting suggests things thrown into turmoil and disorder, so the letters are mixed up

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An irregular soldier is in combat in ancient Sparta.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' looks like a link placing the fighter, but its letters belong to the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A partisan is a member of an irregular armed band resisting an occupying force, the same thing as a guerrilla.

indicators.note: out here means put out of order or out of place, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
A is the indefinite article, meaning one

explanation.surface: Hens begin to lay, one at a time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Layers' tempts as hens; it is the plural of stratum.
explanation.definitionFit: Strata are beds of rock or levels in a society, each one lying on top of another as horizontal layers.

blocks.note: first meaning: a small wading sandpiper of northern coasts
second meaning: a tangled problem, as in being tied up in one

explanation.surface: A bird is in serious trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: The knot is a stocky shorebird, and a knot is also an intricate tangle or problem that is hard to resolve.

blocks.note: surface reading: to come first in a race or contest
setter's reading: a finish is a final treatment or look, and this one is applied to the top of the head

explanation.surface: Someone wins, coming out first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Finish on top' sounds like winning; read literally it is the way the hair on someone's head is cut and arranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A hairstyle is the dressed, cut arrangement given to the hair, a final look applied to the crown of the head.

clue.text: Where to keep playing in London

definitions.text: Where to keep playing in London

blocks.clueFragment: Where to keep playing in London
blocks.note: surface reading: a venue in the capital where you can go on playing a game
setter's reading: a two-word phrase for continuing to perform on stage, run together, is a west London district

explanation.surface: Looking for somewhere in the capital to carry on a game.
explanation.walkthrough: Acton is a district of west London; split as ACT ON, it means to carry on performing.
explanation.definitionFit: The place name is a suburb in the west of the capital, and its two halves describe an actor continuing a performance.

blocks.note: pro means for, in favour of
Il Duce, 'the leader', was the title Mussolini took

explanation.surface: Something that gave the Italian dictator a chance or excuse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Occasion' looks like a noun but is the verb, to cause or bring about.
explanation.definitionFit: To occasion an effect is to cause or bring it about, which is what producing a result means.

blocks.note: first meaning: to draw out or obtain, as information or a tooth
second meaning: a piece clipped from a newspaper or a passage taken from a book

explanation.surface: An instruction to get a move on, or to start slicing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get cutting' reads as one phrase urging haste; split it into a verb and a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: To extract is to obtain by pulling out, and an extract is a press clipping or excerpt taken from a longer text.

clue.text: Subject those people to second degree

indicators.note: second tells us to keep only the letter in position two of the word that follows

blocks.note: them is the pronoun for those people
the second letter of the word degree

explanation.surface: Putting a group of people through a harsh interrogation, the second degree.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface echoes 'third degree', rough questioning, but 'second' only picks a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The theme of a talk or essay is its topic, the subject that it treats or discusses.

clue.text: Where to find the remainder of the market?

definitions.text: Where to find the remainder of the market?

blocks.clueFragment: Where to find the remainder of the market?
blocks.note: surface reading: where are the leftover goods or the rest of the market stalls?
setter's reading: a remainder is an unsold book sold off cheaply, so look for the stall that sells books

explanation.surface: A shopper asks where the rest of the market has gone.
explanation.walkthrough: In the book trade, remainders are surplus copies sold at a reduced price, and they turn up on a book stand in a market.
explanation.definitionFit: A bookstall is a stand or kiosk selling books, often secondhand or cut-price unsold copies in street markets.

blocks.note: a brain is a clever person, an expert
a shaver is an old word for a young lad, a child; the 's links on

explanation.surface: A skilled barber's own creation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shaver' is not a barber but an informal old word for a boy, as in 'little shaver'.
explanation.definitionFit: A brainchild is an idea or invention that someone has originated, an original creation of their mind.

blocks.note: lake is a crimson pigment, as in crimson lake
geneva is an old name for gin, from Dutch genever

explanation.surface: A sea of reddish gin, perhaps a cocktail spill.
explanation.walkthrough: Both pieces are uncommon senses: lake as a red dye and geneva as gin.
explanation.definitionFit: The large body of fresh water between Switzerland and France is a broad watery expanse.

clue.text: Device used for keeping team player in Rugby

blocks.note: a combination is a group working together, a team
a lock is a second-row forward in rugby

explanation.surface: Some apparatus for retaining a squad member at Rugby School.
explanation.walkthrough: Rugby with a capital is the town and school where the game began; a lock is a forward in the scrum's second row.
explanation.definitionFit: A combination lock secures a safe or case, opened only by a set sequence of numbers, so it keeps things safe.

indicators.note: an ordeal puts something through torment and rough treatment, so the word is knocked into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Some westerners suffer a harsh experience in Siberia.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the S moves: it shifts from the front of Siberian to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Iberians are people of the Iberian peninsula, Spaniards and Portuguese, who live in south-west Europe.

clue.text: They could make rusty an animal with its DNA modified

indicators.note: modified means altered, so the letters before it are changed into a new order

blocks.note: an ox is a bovine animal
taken as written

explanation.surface: Genetic engineering on a beast is presented as making it rusty.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface sounds like genetic modification, but 'its DNA' is just six letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Oxidising agents bring about oxidation, which is how iron corrodes into rust in damp air.

indicators.note: potential points to what something could become, so these letters can be made into another word

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Officers who show the makings of greatness.
explanation.definitionFit: Sergeants are police officers of the rank above constable, so they are policemen.

indicators.note: out suggests something wrong or disordered, so these letters are scrambled

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A monkey dashes off.
explanation.definitionFit: The rhesus macaque is a brown South Asian monkey widely used in medical research.

blocks.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps
ling is a long-bodied fish of the cod family

explanation.surface: A hug from an unfriendly, unemotional person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cold fish' is a stock phrase for an aloof person, but here the two words separate.
explanation.definitionFit: To cling to someone is to hold them tightly, much as an embrace does.

clue.text: Chain with more processing shows brilliant finish

indicators.note: processing means working material over, so these letters are worked into a new order

blocks.note: ch is the abbreviation for chain, an old measure of length
taken as written

explanation.surface: Factory work on a chain gives it a gleaming surface.
explanation.walkthrough: A chain is an old surveyor's measure of 22 yards, abbreviated ch.
explanation.definitionFit: Chrome plating gives metal a shiny, mirror-like coating, a bright, gleaming surface treatment.

indicators.note: misbehaving means acting out of line, so the letters do not keep their proper order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone called Fleming is behaving badly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fleming' looks like a surname, perhaps the novelist or the scientist; a Fleming is a native of Flanders.
explanation.definitionFit: A Fleming comes from Flanders, so something belonging to a Fleming is Flemish, the matching adjective.

indicators.note: In tells us the letters sit inside the words that follow, running across the gap between them

blocks.note: the last letter of one word and the start of the next

explanation.surface: Something done for charity earns America a good name.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase 'in aid of' reads as one unit, but 'In' signals the hiding place; 'aid' is padding that keeps the surface smooth.
explanation.definitionFit: Fame is the state of being widely known, renown or a public name, close to a good reputation.

blocks.note: the Bar is the collective name for barristers
a gain is a profit

explanation.surface: Lawyers pocketing their earnings dishonestly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Steal' is the noun, as in 'it was a steal at that price'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that is a steal costs far less than its worth, which is what a bargain is.

indicators.note: sounding means as heard when spoken, so we want a word that matches another in speech

blocks.note: to bate is to lessen or dull, as in bated breath

explanation.surface: A needle whose point has gone dull.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Needle' looks like a noun but it is the verb, to tease or provoke.
explanation.definitionFit: To needle someone is to goad and annoy them, and to bait them is to torment them deliberately.

indicators.note: a cocktail is a mixture, so the letters are mixed together into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone is enthusiastic about a rum-based drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keen on' reads as fond of, but 'Keen' alone is the verb, to wail in grief.
explanation.definitionFit: To keen is to wail in lamentation for the dead, an expression of grief for a loss.

clue.text: Live tomtit almost fluttering at this musical 13

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the final letter of the bird is left off
fluttering is a restless, darting movement, so the letters are tossed into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
the small bird's name without its last letter

explanation.surface: A live bird flapping about inspires a piece of music.
explanation.walkthrough: 13 refers to the answer at 13 across, THEME, so the definition is a musical theme.
explanation.definitionFit: A leitmotiv is a recurring musical phrase tied to a character or idea, as in Wagner's operas.
